\begin{abstract}
Do demographic personas improve an LLM's prediction of audience engagement? We compare a fixed
ten-persona panel with a generic-reader baseline on Upworthy headlines, with supplementary
news and Reddit comparisons. The primary experiment collects Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite and GPT-4.1
observations on the same \newSelectedN{}-package exploratory cohort, selected with simultaneous
winner screening. It allocates thirty scores per arm and variant within model, retains exact raw
responses, and reports metric-specific valid and paired counts. Complete-package coverage is
\newGeminiN{} for Gemini and \newGptN{} for GPT-4.1. The baseline-minus-panel Kendall $\tau_b$ gap is
\newGeminiGapTau{} (CI [\newGeminiGapTauLow{}, \newGeminiGapTauHigh{}]) for Gemini and
\newGptGapTau{} (CI [\newGptGapTauLow{}, \newGptGapTauHigh{}]) for GPT-4.1, on respectively
\newGeminiPairedTauN{} and \newGptPairedTauN{} valid rank pairs. Expected top-1 is
\newGeminiPanelTopOne{} versus \newGeminiBaselineTopOne{} for Gemini and \newGptPanelTopOne{}
versus \newGptBaselineTopOne{} for GPT-4.1 (panel versus baseline). These intervals condition on
the selected cohort and recorded generations and do not adjust for dependence between related experiments. The Upworthy archive documents a randomization-risk
period. Excluding that period in a post-hoc sensitivity retains positive expected top-1 and lift
gaps in both configurations, while Gemini tau-b and Spearman intervals include zero. Supplementary
Reddit top-1 and captured lift favor the panel; these aggregate comparisons use unreconciled
collection protocols and do not isolate dataset effects. A raw-replay artifact supports offline reproduction of the primary experiment.
The results concern this panel, cohort, and protocol; they are not a held-out evaluation or
evidence of universal persona harm. Provider request protocols differ across models, and no
causal mechanism is isolated.
\end{abstract}

\section{Sim-to-Real Validity Framework}
A package contains variants with observed outcome rates and predicted scores
(Figure~\ref{fig:protocol}). Upworthy was designed for randomized traffic, but the archive authors document randomization
problems during part of 2013--2014~\citep{matias2024correction}. We report observed rate rankings;
they are not automatically causal headline effects. Grouping distinct headlines can also combine
image variants. MIND ranks different articles within a subcategory by clicks divided by logged
article appearances, pooling user-level recommendation logs. Reddit groups reposts by image and
subreddit, pools votes for identical titles, and uses upvotes divided by total upvotes plus
downvotes. This is a vote-approval ratio, not CTR; vote totals are not exposure counts. Timing,
recommendation, and exposure remain uncontrolled in these observational comparisons.
\input{figures/protocol}
Within-package ranking does not establish absolute CTR calibration or a causal copy effect
in observational data.

\paragraph{Metric identity.}
For concordant and discordant pair counts $C,D$, Goodman--Kruskal gamma is
\[
\gamma=(C-D)/(C+D),
\]
discarding pairs tied in either variable~\citep{goodman1954}. It is undefined when $C+D=0$ and
differs from Kendall $\tau_b$, which accounts for ties:
\[
\tau_b=\frac{C-D}{\sqrt{(C+D+T_x)(C+D+T_y)}},
\]
where $T_x,T_y$ count pairs tied only in the respective variable~\citep{kendall1945ties}.
Spearman uses average ranks~\citep{spearman1904}. Constant rank inputs yield undefined values.

\paragraph{Elicitation and aggregation.}
The prompt requests JSON with a \texttt{click\_intent} number in $[0,1]$
(Appendix~\ref{sec:appendix}). Scores are averaged across recorded observations:
\[
\widehat{s}(v)=\frac{1}{|O_v|}\sum_{(i,d)\in O_v}y_{i,d}(v).
\]
With complete draws this equals the mean over personas and draws. With missing draws it can
differ from the supplementary aggregation mean, which weights draw-collapsed personas equally. The supplementary aggregation comparison evaluates these alternative rules.

\paragraph{Simultaneous winner screen.}
The primary experiment requires a unique observed maximum and compares it with every opponent using
two-sided pooled $z$ tests. For $k$ variants the comparison family contains $m=k(k-1)/2$ unordered
pairs. All winner--opponent comparisons must pass $\alpha/m$, with $\alpha=0.05$.
The screening statistic is $\min(1,m\max_{j\ne w}p_{wj})$. Bonferroni's inequality motivates the
adjustment~\citep{nistBonferroni}. The nominal bound is approximate and per package, conditional on
independent binomial observations, fixed sampling horizons, and adequate normal approximation. It is not an across-package
false-discovery guarantee or proof of a population winner. Repeated exposures and Reddit voting
further limit these assumptions. In the locked corpus \newSelectedN{} packages pass, all within
the supplementary selected set described below. A stricter screen does not demonstrate that removed packages had
false winners. The archive documents editorial stopping based on accumulating results~\citep{matiasUpworthy}.
Fixed-horizon $p$-values need not remain calibrated under that stopping policy; Bonferroni does
not repair invalid input $p$-values. The screen defines a reproducible cohort, without a verified
five-percent winner-error guarantee for these archived tests.

\paragraph{Estimation and denominators.}
Primary package metrics are averaged without size weighting. The displayed means describe the recorded
packages. Bootstrap intervals summarize between-package resampling variability conditional on
the selection rule and recorded scores; interpreting them for a population of similarly selected
experiments additionally assumes that these packages are exchangeable independent units. Raw-backed reports include
$n_{\mathrm{total}},n_{\mathrm{valid}},n_{\mathrm{undefined}}$ and metric-specific package IDs.
Each paired gap uses packages valid in both arms for that metric. Empty estimates are undefined,
not zero. Primary and period-exclusion percentile bootstrap CIs use $10{,}000$ package resamples, seed $42$
\citep{efron1979bootstrap}. They condition on selection and recorded scores and omit generation,
selection, and outcome-measurement uncertainty. These are pointwise estimation intervals, not
simultaneous guarantees across metrics or models. Resampling treats experiment IDs as independent
units. The archive also records follow-up tests with shared content~\citep{matiasUpworthy};
related IDs may therefore be dependent. The intervals do not adjust for such dependence, and
their coverage as population confidence intervals is not established. Supplementary aggregate coefficient-specific valid counts
are not fully recorded; coverage totals are not those denominators.

\section{Discussion and Limitations}
The comparisons make a generic-reader baseline necessary for this task. A persona panel adds
assumptions about audience composition and behavior that require predictive validation.
The primary matched-score comparisons favor the baseline in valid rank comparisons, expected top-1
and captured lift, but do not establish a bottom-1 advantage. Gemini rank means exclude constant
outputs with explicit arm-specific counts; top-1 retains those packages through expected tie
credit. Supplementary Upworthy reports and the GPT checkpoint analysis also favor the baseline;
supplementary Reddit decision metrics favor the panel. Excluding the documented randomization-risk
period preserves the primary top-1 and lift contrasts but leaves Gemini tau-b and Spearman uncertain.
The ranking conclusion therefore depends on cohort and estimator, not just model configuration.

\paragraph{Mechanism remains open.}
The baseline may use general headline knowledge, while role-play may add unhelpful conditioning.
Neither explanation was isolated experimentally. Similar score spreads, selected ranking examples,
and rank-only aggregation failures cannot distinguish bias from noise or identify a mechanism.
The balanced, interleaved primary collection tests the panel/baseline comparison with retained raw
responses, but does not separately manipulate demographic content, role-play, or response noise.

\citep{matias2024correction}; our selected cohort includes affected-window tests. Our predictions
rank recorded outcome rates, and neither an adjusted screen nor model responses establishes
causal headline effects. The post-hoc exclusion sensitivity addresses one known risk window,
not every possible allocation or image confound. Editorial stopping and shared content across
follow-up experiments~\citep{matiasUpworthy} add distinct risks: the screen does not correct
sequential monitoring, and the package bootstrap does not cluster related experiment IDs.

has not been quantified by an article-level cluster analysis. Nominal intervals may understate
uncertainty. Simultaneous screening does not make outcome measurements certain. Exclusion changes the target population and relative task difficulty.
Failure to reject equality does not imply no predictor can recover an ordering.
MIND and Reddit are observational; correlated exposures, time, image, audience mix, and topic
may matter. Training contamination and generalization to current audiences or other formats
are not excluded by the archive corpus.
